title: Model Release Selector & Performance Ledger
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a clear, compact console flow for selecting a model release (candidate), comparing it to the current production release, pinning a release for a route, and publishing a curated performance profile (the 'performance ledger') that teams can browse and attach to rollouts. This should support quick QA decisions and safe rollout practices without requiring engineers to jump between pages or external dashboards.

User problems to solve:
- PM/engineer onboarding a new model release needs a single view to compare latency/cost/quality signals and decide whether to pin or schedule a rollout.
- Console currently exposes model versions and raw perf snapshots separately; users get lost copying numbers between tabs.
- Non-engineering stakeholders need a discoverable record of published performance profiles for audits and postmortems.

Primary user flows:
1) Model list -> select model -> open "Release Selector" panel shows current production release (left) and candidate release (right) with side-by-side metrics.
2) Compare mode: inline micro-charts (p95 latency, median throughput, cost per 1k tokens, eval accuracy on selected test suite) + qualitative notes.
3) Quick actions: Pin to route (dropdown of routes), Schedule canary (config modal), Publish performance ledger entry (title, summary, attached benchmark run, optional eval results).
4) Ledger browsing: searchable list of published ledger entries per model with tags, author, date, and link to the originating benchmark run and PR.

Design notes / UI components required:
- Compact two-column comparison card with small sparkline for trend and three key KPI badges.
- Pin indicator (locked icon + tooltip) visible wherever release is shown.
- "Publish Ledger" modal that collects a short narrative, links to artifacts (GitHub PR, benchmark run), and optional quality gate checkboxes.
- Lightweight inline diff view for eval outputs (textual/regression examples).

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Done):
- AC1: From model detail page, user can open Release Selector and see current prod vs candidate with at least 4 KPIs (latency p95, median latency, cost/1k tokens, eval score) pulled from the perf backend.
- AC2: User can pin a candidate release to one of the model's routes; pin action writes to the route config and creates an audit entry.
- AC3: User can publish a performance ledger entry that persists a title, summary, artifact links, and optional tags; entry appears in the model's ledger list.
- AC4: Ledger list supports search by tag/author and sorting by date; clicking a ledger entry surfaces the original comparison snapshot and links to PR/benchmark.
- AC5: All actions are guarded by RBAC: only users with route-modify permission see Pin controls.

Instrumentation and telemetry:
- Events: release_selector.open, release_selector.compare_viewed, release_selector.pin_clicked, release_selector.schedule_canary, ledger.publish, ledger.view, ledger.search.
- Properties: model_id, candidate_version, prod_version, route_id (if applicable), user_role, result_of_quality_gate.

Dependencies:
- Perf backend API to return canonical KPI set for a version (latency percentiles, cost estimates, eval scores) (ENG-2410).
- RBAC checks for route modification and ledger publish actions (ENG-2558).
- Design deliverables (Figma mockups) and copy doc.

Rollout plan:
1) Beta behind feature flag scoped to internal orgs + pilot customers (console-2026.03).
2) Validate telemetry for decisions and collect qualitative feedback from 3 pilot teams.
3) Iterate on ledger fields (add more tags/structured fields) before wider release.

QA and testing notes:
- Verify read/write of pin operation persists to route config and appears in audit logs.
- Validate published ledger entries are immutable except for a 15-minute edit window.
- Accessibility: Ensure comparison card is keyboard navigable and charts have alt text summaries.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should the ledger entry automatically snapshot the full eval outputs or only a link to benchmark storage? (proposed: snapshot summary + optional attach full run if <= 5MB).
- What quality gates should be toggled by default for non-engineer roles? (Design to propose).

Artifacts / links:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/Model+Release+Selector
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/model-release-selector (WIP)
- Example PR pattern: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2042

Out-of-scope for initial iteration:
- Automatic suggestion of candidate versions based on cost/latency heuristics (future).
- Full multi-armed bandit rollout engine integration (future).
